question.problem: What is the equation of the line that passes through the points $(0,0)$ and $(4,7)$, expressed in standard form?
question.worked_solution:
First, we will construct the point-slope form of the line. Then, we will simplify it into standard form.

To construct the point-slope form of the line, we need a point and a slope. We already have two points, so we calculate the slope $m$ using the given points:

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}=\frac{7-0}{4-0}=\frac{7}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use this slope along with one of the points to write the point-slope form equation of the line. It doesn't matter which point we choose, but let's choose $(0,0).$ The point-slope equation is as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-0 & =\frac{7}{4}(x-0) \\ y & =\frac{7}{4}x\end{aligned}
$$

To simplify the point-slope formula into standard form, we first multiply by $4$ to get rid of the fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{7}{4}(x) \\ 4\cdot (y) & =4\cdot \frac{7}{4}(x) \\ 4y & =7x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we move the variables to the left side and the constant to the right side:

$$
\begin{aligned}4y & =7x \\ -7x+4y & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply by $-1$ to make the $x$-coefficient positive:

$$
\begin{aligned}-7x+4y & =0 \\ (-1)\cdot (-7x+4y) & =(-1)\cdot 0 \\ 7x-4y & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the standard form of the equation is $7x-4y=0.$
